samples.summary: Nothing tests that erasing/logging out drops the per-account device secret
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineData` ends with `forgetDeviceSecret(userId)` (offline-erase.ts:39), documented as load-bearing: the salt is the one ingredient of `wb:{deviceSecret}:{userId}:{docKey}` a later signed-in user of a shared device cannot otherwise obtain, and Yorkie authorises ActivateClient/DeactivateClient on token validity alone. `src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts` never reads `localStorage['wafflebase-durable-device:*']`, never imports `forgetDeviceSecret` or `durableClientKey`, and never asserts anything about the secret in the `erasing` or `signing out` describes. `durable-session.test.ts:127` tests `forgetDeviceSecret` in isolation, which passes regardless of whether the erase calls it. Deleting line 39 leaves the whole suite green while the guard silently disappears.
searchedFor: read src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts (erasing / signing out / watching-the-preference blocks)

samples.summary: The DurabilityLapse values the durable client publishes are asserted by no test
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` maps its latched state onto `dropped` / `too-large` / `out-of-space` / `write-failed` / `unreportable` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:215-225), and the `QuotaExceededError` → `setOutOfSpace(true)` branch at :164-169 is the only producer of `out-of-space`. `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx`'s only consumer is `Probe`, which reads `useDocumentDurability()` — a boolean — so every one of those five strings, and the quota branch, can be deleted or reordered without a failing test. A grep for `useDurabilityLapse|out-of-space|too-large` across packages/frontend matches only the source files plus `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx`, which builds `DurabilityLapseScope`s by hand rather than mounting the provider. The design requirement this serves ("its tooltip must name which case applies") is therefore unverified at the point where the reason is produced.

samples.summary: CollabDocumentProvider's lapse computation and the scope-placement fix have no regression test
samples.evidence: Lines 291-299 compute `unsupported` / `not-permitted` / `not-enabled` / `another-tab`, and the comment at the `DurabilityLapseScope` (line 350) records that mounting the scope inside `inner` was a shipped bug which overwrote every reason the durable client publishes. `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` asserts only `mounted` props, lock state and child identity — it never renders a lapse consumer, and a grep shows the file contains no reference to `useDurabilityLapse` or `DurabilityLapseScope`. Moving the scope back inside `inner`, or breaking the four-way lapse ternary, fails nothing. The only lapse assertions live in the chip suite, where both scopes are constructed by hand.
searchedFor: grep useDurabilityLapse|DurabilityLapseScope across packages/frontend (6 files, no durable provider tests)

samples.summary: The new `saved-locally` tooltip sentence is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: `tooltipFor` gains a `saved-locally` branch whose wording is deliberate ("will be sent when syncing resumes", not "when the connection returns", because the state is also reached while connected). Every `tooltipFor(...)` call in `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` passes `'not-saved'` (line 784) or `'saved'` (line 836); no test passes `'saved-locally'`, and the durable chip tests assert the label and the toast rather than the tooltip. The branch — including the `pendingSince` timestamp arm — can return anything without failing a test.

samples.summary: No test covers recovery out of `saved-locally` (the latched info toast being retracted and confirmed)
samples.evidence: The new `savedLocally` arm sets `warned.current = true` (chip line 190) specifically so the recovery arm below retracts the info toast and confirms once the work reaches the server. The durable chip tests in `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` only drive the forward transition (`says where the work went instead of saying nothing`) and never move the state on to `saved`, so `toast.dismiss(TOAST_ID)` / the `Saved` confirmation after a `saved-locally` episode is unasserted — as is the unmount cleanup for that latch. A regression would leave a stale "Saved to this device" notification with no confirmation, which no test would catch.
searchedFor: read tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx 'SyncStatusChip on a durable document' block

samples.summary: The cross-account guard on the orphan-snapshot sweep is never exercised
samples.evidence: `orphanSnapshotKeys()` filters with `!this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)` (line 1295), whose regex parses `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` out of the store key (line 1315). The only orphan test — `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts`, "an entry that predates the header rule" — seeds the key `"doc-a"`, which matches the regex not at all, so the guard is inert there. A grep for `belongsToAnotherUser` or a `wb:`-shaped orphan key across `src/lib` finds no test. Both failure directions are silent: a regex that never matches lets one account's sweep delete another's orphan rows, and one that over-matches leaves orphans permanently uncollectable while still holding document content.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts 'an entry that predates the header rule'

samples.summary: "accepts an id as readily as a slug" does not exercise the id branch it names
samples.evidence: `documentIdsIn` matches on `document.workspaceId === ref || (!!workspace && document.workspaceId === workspace.id)`. The test at workspaces.test.ts:91 calls `deleteWorkspace("ws-uuid")` with `mockFetch.mockResolvedValue(okJson(WORKSPACE))`, so `fetchWorkspace` resolves `{ id: "ws-uuid" }` and the *second* disjunct already matches `d1`. Deleting the `document.workspaceId === ref` term leaves this test green, so the branch the test is named for — the fallback used when the workspace lookup fails (which `documentIdsIn` explicitly tolerates via `.catch(() => undefined)`) — is uncovered. Making `fetchWorkspace` reject in this case would make the assertion match its title.

samples.summary: `keepArchives` (and `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser`) have no caller and no test
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (line 1123/1161) is documented as existing for the expired-session path, but after the `eraseLocalData: "none"` decision that path erases nothing at all: a grep for `keepArchives` across packages/frontend/src finds only the option's declaration in offline-erase.ts:30 and the store, never a call passing `true`. `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` parameter is likewise never supplied by either call site. Neither branch is reachable from any test, so both are untested dead options that a future caller could wire up wrongly with nothing to catch it.
searchedFor: read dropAllForUser and dropArchivesWhere in src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `eraseOfflineData` does call `forgetDeviceSecret(userId)` at offline-erase.ts:39, and it is the only production call site of that function. I read offline-erase.test.ts in full: no assertion anywhere observes the per-account device secret — the erasing/preference/logout blocks check only `store.load`, `listArchives`, `isOfflineWritePermitted`, and the `wafflebase-offline-user` mirror (line 670). Searching beyond the reviewer's paths: a repo-wide grep for `deviceSecret|device-secret|DEVICE_SECRET` yields test hits only in durable-session.test.ts and a prose comment in collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:160 (whose test asserts clientKey shape at mount, lines 164-165, and never erases); a repo-wide grep for `eraseOfflineData(OnLogout)?` yields only api/auth.ts and tests/api/auth.test.ts, which mocks the entire offline-erase module (tests/api/auth.test.ts:87-89) and asserts only `expect(erase).toHaveBeenCalled()` (line 110); and grepping packages/frontend/tests for `wafflebase-durable-device|forgetDeviceSecret|clientKey` returns nothing. durable-session.test.ts:123-134 is titled "forgets an account's secret when its data is erased" but invokes `forgetDeviceSecret` directly, so it passes whether or not the erase path calls it — it reads as coverage without being it. Deleting offline-erase.ts:39 leaves the suite green while a shared-device privacy guard (per docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:383-389) silently disappears: major, no counterexample found.
